outcomes.text: Explain the creation narratives.
Compare different interpretations of the Genesis text.
Examine relationships between religious and scientific creation views.
Explain the doctrines of the fall and original sin and their importance in Christian thought.
Describe God’s nature as portrayed in Genesis 1–3.
Describe the relationship between God and humanity in the text.
Explain Christian teachings about environmental care and stewardship from the text.
Relate Genesis 1–3 to Christian belief and practice today.
Explain Abram’s call and God’s promises to him.
Describe how the covenant was formed.
Explain the covenant’s place in God’s plan for humanity.
Explain circumcision as the covenant’s sign.
Describe God’s testing of Abraham.
Describe the relationship between God and his people in the texts.
Explain how God is depicted as communicating with creation.
Describe God’s nature as portrayed in the texts.
Relate these texts to Christian belief and practice today.
Explain Moses and the Exodus narrative.
Explain God’s liberation of his people from slavery in Egypt.
Explain how God reveals himself, including through his name.
Explain how God acts through miracles.
Explain symbolic links between Passover and the Eucharist.
Explain how Passover and Exodus inform Christian salvation beliefs.
Describe God’s nature as portrayed in the texts.
Describe the relationship between God and his people in the texts.
Relate these texts to Christian belief and practice today.
Explain how God chose and appointed David.
Explain calling or vocation in Christian thought.
Explain the account of David and Goliath.
Explain the king’s role as God’s earthly representative.
Explain God’s covenant with David.
Explain the promised Messiah as David’s descendant.
Explain Christian belief that Jesus is the Messiah.
Describe God’s nature and relationship with his people in the texts.
Relate these texts to Christian belief and practice today.
Explain Isaiah’s prophecy concerning injustice.
Explain how prophets challenge injustice and express God’s compassion.
Explain prophets’ roles in proclaiming God’s word and future events.
Explain Isaiah’s prophecy concerning the Messiah.
Describe Christian beliefs about Jesus as a prophet.
Explain Isaiah’s prophecy of the suffering servant.
Explain the Christian identification of the suffering servant with Jesus.
Explain Jonah as a prophet improving society by proclaiming God’s word.
Explain Jonah’s teachings about God’s nature and relationship with his people.
Relate these texts to Christian belief and practice today.
Compare how Jesus was proclaimed to different audiences, including gentiles.
Explain Jesus as saviour fulfilling Old Testament prophecy.
Explain how Jesus’ death and resurrection were communicated to different audiences.
Explain Christian teachings about the afterlife in 1 Corinthians.
Describe God’s nature and relationship with his people in the texts.
Relate these texts to Christian belief and practice today.

topics.title: Topic 7 The Holy Spirit as guide

outcomes.text: Explain how the Holy Spirit equipped the early church for evangelism.
Explain Peter’s Pentecost speech.
Compare Peter’s encounter with Cornelius and Philip’s encounter with the Ethiopian eunuch.
Explain the role of visions in the early church and Christianity today.
Explain the Holy Spirit’s role in the early church and modern Christians’ lives.
Explain baptism as the beginning of Christian community membership.
Describe God’s nature and relationship with his people in the texts.
Relate these texts to Christian belief and practice today.

units.title: Paper 2 The Portrayal of Jesus in the Synoptic Gospels

topics.title: Topic 1 The political and religious background to the life and times of Jesus

outcomes.text: Explain Jewish rule during Jesus’ lifetime.
Explain Roman rule during Jesus’ lifetime.
Describe the Zealots.
Describe the gentiles.
Describe the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Explain the roles of the temple and synagogue.
Explain Jewish Messianic hopes during Jesus’ time.
Compare how each Synoptic Gospel portrays Jesus.
Explain the readership and purpose of each Synoptic Gospel.

topics.title: Topic 2 Key events in the life of Jesus until the transfiguration

outcomes.text: Know Matthew’s accounts of Jesus’ birth and infancy.
Know Luke’s accounts of Jesus’ birth and infancy.
Study the story of the boy Jesus in the temple.
Study Jesus’ baptism and its significance.
Study Jesus’ temptation in the wilderness.
Study John the Baptist’s proclamation and imprisonment.
Study Jesus’ rejection at Nazareth.
Study Peter’s declaration that Jesus is the Messiah.
Study Jesus’ prediction of his death and resurrection.
Study Jesus’ transfiguration.
Explain the significance and modern Christian relevance of the studied events.
Explain how the texts show God’s plan for humanity and John the Baptist’s importance.

topics.title: Topic 3 Key events in the last week of Jesus’ life, including his resurrection and ascension

outcomes.text: Study Jesus’ triumphal entry into Jerusalem.
Study the Lord’s Supper, Jesus’ betrayal and his arrest.
Study Peter’s denial of Jesus.
Study Jesus’ trial before the high priest.
Study Jesus’ trial before Pilate.
Study Jesus’ crucifixion and death.
Study Jesus’ burial.
Study Matthew’s resurrection accounts.
Study Luke’s resurrection accounts.
Study Jesus’ ascension.
Explain the meaning and present-day Christian relevance of the studied events.
Explain how these events contribute to God’s plan for humanity through Jesus’ resurrection and ascension.

topics.title: Topic 4 Conflict and opposition to Jesus

outcomes.text: Study the Sabbath controversy in Mark.
Study the Sabbath controversies recorded by Luke.
Study opposition to Jesus from the Pharisees.
Study Jesus’ cleansing of the Temple.
Study the plot to kill Jesus in Matthew.
Explain the sources and reasons for opposition to Jesus and his response.
Explain how these texts portray Jesus’ person and work.
Explain the relevance of these texts for Christian belief and practice today.
Explain how these texts may reveal aspects of God’s plan for humanity.
Study nature miracles, including the calming of the storm, feeding the five thousand and walking on water.
Study healing miracles involving a paralytic, a centurion’s servant, a sick woman and a Syrophoenician woman.
Study Jesus’ exorcisms of the Gerasene man and a demon-possessed boy.
Study Jesus raising the widow’s son at Nain and restoring a girl to life.
Study how miracles relate to the kingdom of God.
Explain how miracles indicate Jesus’ power, ministry, the kingdom of God and identity.
Explain the relevance of these miracle accounts for Christian belief and practice today.
Explain how these miracle accounts may reveal aspects of God’s plan for humanity.
Understand the kingdom of God in Jesus’ teaching.
Study parables about preparing for the kingdom, including the sower, good Samaritan, rich fool, and rich man and Lazarus.
Study parables about receiving the kingdom, including the lost sheep, lost coin, prodigal son, and talents.
Study parables about acting in the kingdom, including the great dinner, vineyard labourers, and ten bridesmaids.
Explain why Jesus taught in parables and what they reveal about his person and work.
Explain the meanings of the parables.
Explain what the kingdom of God means within Jesus’ teaching.
Explain the relevance of these parables for Christian belief and practice today.
Explain how these parables may reveal aspects of God’s plan for humanity.

topics.title: Topic 7 The teachings and sayings of Jesus

outcomes.text: Study the teachings and duties presented in the Sermon on the Mount.
Study Jesus’ teaching on prayer, including the Lord’s Prayer and perseverance in prayer.
Explain how these teachings reveal aspects of Jesus’ person and work.
Explain the relevance of these teachings for Christian belief and practice today.
Explain how these teachings may reveal aspects of God’s plan for humanity.
